turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve had persistent fatigue for about two months, with a few episodes of lower abdominal pain that haven’t improved even after two weeks off work. I’m also very stressed and I’m worried it could be something serious like cancer, so I’d like to discuss getting more definitive tests.
Can you describe the character of the abdominal pain—its exact location, quality (sharp, dull, cramping), and whether anything seems to make it better or worse?

Patient: The lower abdominal pain is mostly in the lower central/pelvic area, more crampy than sharp, and it comes and goes—there’s no clear trigger, and rest or my usual routine doesn’t really make it better. I can’t say it’s linked to meals, bowel movements, or my period, and it just seems to persist despite being off work.
Do you notice any changes in your bowel habits—such as diarrhea, constipation, blood or mucus in the stool, or a feeling of incomplete evacuation?
Patient: I haven’t noticed diarrhea or constipation, and I haven’t seen any blood or mucus in my stool. I also don’t feel like I’m not emptying completely after I go.
Have you had any urinary symptoms such as increased frequency, urgency, burning on urination, or blood in the urine?
Patient: No, I haven’t had any burning, urgency, or increased frequency, and I haven’t noticed any blood in my urine.
Are you experiencing any other systemic symptoms such as fever, night sweats, unintended weight loss, loss of appetite, or feeling unusually cold?

Patient: I don’t have fever or night sweats, but I feel unusually tired and pale, and I’ve had generalized weakness in my proximal muscles. I’ve also felt more down than usual, but my appetite hasn’t clearly changed and I haven’t noticed unintended weight loss.
Can you tell me about your menstrual cycle—how regular it is, how long it lasts, and whether your periods are heavier or lighter than usual?

Patient: My menstrual cycle has been pretty regular, and the bleeding isn’t noticeably heavier or lighter than usual—I haven’t seen any significant change in how long my period lasts. I can’t say the pelvic pain tracks with my period either; it seems to come and go regardless.
Do you ever notice heavier or longer menstrual bleeding than you used to, or need to change pads/tampons more frequently because of the flow?

Patient: No, my periods haven’t been heavier or lasting longer, and I’m not having to change pads or tampons more frequently than before. I can’t tell that the pelvic pain lines up with my cycle either.

Patient: I don’t follow a special diet—I eat a fairly normal mixed diet. I haven’t noticed any particular foods that reliably worsen the fatigue or the pelvic pain. My appetite is roughly the same, though I’ve been under a lot of stress.

Patient: I haven’t had a pregnancy test recently, and I can’t rule pregnancy out—what tests would you recommend first? I’m able to do it right away if you want, since I’ve been feeling persistently unwell.
Are you sexually active, and if so, what form of contraception do you use (if any)?

Patient: Yes, I’m sexually active, and I use contraception consistently—so pregnancy risk is low, but I can still do a pregnancy test now if you think it’s important. I’ve also not noticed any unusual vaginal discharge or bleeding changes.
Do you notice any increased sensitivity to cold, dry skin, hair thinning, constipation, or unexplained weight gain that have developed over the past few months?

Patient: I haven’t really noticed constipation, weight gain, or hair thinning, and I don’t feel particularly cold. I’ve mainly felt persistently tired and pale with generalized proximal muscle weakness, plus the intermittent pelvic crampy pain.
Are you currently taking any prescription or over‑the‑counter medications, supplements, or herbal products (including iron, multivitamins, or hormonal contraceptives)?

Patient: I’m currently taking omeprazole for my peptic ulcer disease, and I’m not taking any other regular prescription meds, supplements, or herbal products. I’ve only used occasional over-the-counter pain relief as needed for the pelvic discomfort.
Do you ever notice dark, tarry stools or any visible blood in your stool, even if it’s occasional?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any dark, tarry stools or any visible blood in my stool. I also haven’t seen mucus or any concerning changes in my bowel movements.

Patient: I’m not aware of any family history of anemia, thyroid disease, or bowel/gastrointestinal cancers. I do know my work stress has been high, and I’ve been feeling increasingly pale and weak despite resting.
Have you ever been diagnosed with anemia or had low hemoglobin/hematocrit on a blood test before this recent period of fatigue?

Patient: I haven’t been told I’m anemic before, and I don’t recall any prior low hemoglobin or hematocrit results. But I’ve been feeling very pale and unusually weak for the past couple of months, which is why I’m worried there could be something more going on.
